successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: 'The new lands were incorporated into a province called Gallia Transalpina'; the Allobroges 'kept administrative autonomy and their territory' but paid 'heavy taxes to Rome'

ledger.x: 218 BC: the Allobroges, first dated in the sources, as Hannibal crosses their land.
By 130 BC: the Allobroges hold Genaua (Geneva).
121 BC: Domitius Ahenobarbus fights the Allobroges at Vindalium.
August 121 BC: the Allobroges, Arverni and Saluvii are beaten at the Isère.
121 BC: the Allobrogian country passes to Rome.
121 BC: the independent Allobroges end; their civitas, with Vienna as capital, lives on inside Gallia Transalpina (Gallia Narbonensis).

wars.name: First Transalpine War
wars.outcome: Roman victory: Domitius Ahenobarbus at Vindalium, Fabius Maximus at the Isère in August 121; the Allobroges brought under Rome, Bituitus captured, the Roman province in Transalpine Gaul established.

certainty.note: The page gives the Rhône, the Isère, the Alps and Lake Geneva as natural limits; no treaty or survey line.
